subject: Reference interview: Cedarbrook Clinics — availability, agenda & recording consent
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cedarbrook-clinics.com>
Cc: Tom Chen <t.chen@cedarbrook-clinics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Reference interview: Cedarbrook Clinics — availability, agenda & recording consent

Hi Marta,

Thanks again for agreeing to speak with us — we really appreciate Cedarbrook taking the time. We'd like to record a short (20–30 minute) discovery interview to capture how your team uses Redwood Inference and to highlight the results for a customer reference.

Quick asks so we can get this on the calendar:
- Can you confirm who should join from your side (names/titles)?
- Two 30-minute options we can propose: Tue 11/23 10:00–10:30 AM PT or Wed 11/24 2:00–2:30 PM PT. Do either work?
- Are you comfortable with a recorded session for a short case highlight and internal reference materials? We will share the recording and a write-up for your review before publishing.

Attached is a short questionnaire we usually send ahead (cedarbrook_case_questions_v1.pdf) — no need to fill everything out, just helpful context.

If it helps, Laura (cc'd) will join from our product team to ask a couple of technical clarifying questions, and Marissa from the customer marketing team may help with logistics and approvals.

Thanks — happy to be flexible on timing.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Success Manager
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

---
Attachment: cedarbrook_case_questions_v1.pdf (1 page — discovery prompts)

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cedarbrook-clinics.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Reference interview: Cedarbrook Clinics — availability, agenda & recording consent

Hi Karthik,

Thanks — happy to do this. Attendees from Cedarbrook: Tom Chen (Head of AI Ops) and myself (Director of Clinical Data). We may bring a brief note-taker but won't need any extra hands.

Both time slots are tricky for us because of clinic hours, but Tue 11/23 10:00–10:30 AM PT should work — Tom and I can join that one. We're fine with recording as long as we get to review the write-up before anything is published.

I took a quick look at the questionnaire; we'll fill the first page and bring the rest to the call.

See you Tue.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Director, Clinical Data
Cedarbrook Clinics
marta.ruiz@cedarbrook-clinics.com

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reference interview: Cedarbrook Clinics — availability, agenda & recording consent

Great — thanks for confirming, Marta. I've gone ahead and booked Tue 11/23 10:00–10:30 AM PT and sent a Google Calendar invite (link below).

Proposed 20–25 minute agenda so we stay focused:
1) Quick intros (2 min)
2) High-level use case & outcome (6–8 min)
3) Implementation notes / what surprised you (6–8 min)
4) Results & metrics you'd like highlighted (4–6 min)
5) Next steps & consent to share write-up (2 min)

If you want to add or swap anything, let me know. We'll record the call (for accuracy) and I will follow up with a short draft write-up and the recording for your review.

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=cedarbrook-disc-20261123

Thanks — Laura and Marissa will join.

Best,
Karthik
---
Attachment: cedarbrook_case_questions_v1.pdf (I'm attaching again in case the first email got buried)

From: Tom Chen <t.chen@cedarbrook-clinics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cedarbrook-clinics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2026 10:36:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Reference interview: Cedarbrook Clinics — availability, agenda & recording consent

Thanks — confirmed on our side and we appreciate the concise agenda. One small ask: could you avoid mentioning raw PHI or any patient identifiers in the write-up? We assume you'll redact specifics, but want to make that explicit.

Recording consent: we're fine with the recording for internal use and customer marketing as long as we review the final copy and anything published removes identifiable clinical details.

See you shortly.

—Tom
Head of AI Ops
Cedarbrook Clinics
